editorial.headline: Government Labour Institutions: Closed to Foreign Investment
editorial.standfirst: Government institutions in employment are nationally closed to PMA and cannot be registered for PMA in Bali today.
editorial.body:
For a foreign investor considering Bali, the conclusion is direct: this activity cannot be registered for PMA there today. The national record is also marked TERTUTUP, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 0%. Both positions point in one direction: the record offers no foreign-ownership opening for this activity. That clarity matters because the defined activity concerns the work of government institutions in employment.

KBLI 84148 covers government-institution activity in labour matters. Its stated scope brings together guidance, development and the conduct of functions in the field of employment, with government labour institutions given as the example. Read together, those terms place institutional responsibility at the centre. The three stated functions matter: guidance is part of the scope; so is development; so is the organisation of activity in the employment field. The record identifies both the institution and the field in which it operates, without separating the activity into unnamed services or arrangements. Its wording should be held to that boundary.

That definition also answers who registers it: the identified profile is a government institution operating in employment. No scale is listed as open in the record. It would be wrong to add a small, medium or large classification where none has been supplied; the absence of an open scale is itself the full position available here. The PMA entry is TERTUTUP, and the national foreign-ownership ceiling is 0%. These are not an invitation to seek an unstated exception. They are the complete national position supplied in the record, with Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021 cited as its PMA source.

Bali needs to be read on its own terms, although the result is the same: TERTUTUP. The record expressly marks PMA registration as blocked there. Its stated reason places the activity in the medium-high/high-risk band and says that it is not blocked by the provincial moratorium; it also calls for verification per address. This is a meaningful distinction. The permanent, island-wide Bali moratorium applies to all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, but that is not the stated reason for the block here. The result nevertheless remains firm: a foreigner cannot register this activity for PMA in Bali today.
